output.brief:
The departures are not a general pay, market or billable-target problem. Regulatory Investigations lost 37.5% of its associates, while other groups sit at 11–14%. The target change applied to every group. Of the 13 associates never put on Kestrel, one left. Of the 11 on Kestrel, eight left. Pay would affect both sets of associates, so it does not explain that gap.

What I can't tell you is whether the cause is the Kestrel workload or the way Dorian Faulk supervises. Every Kestrel associate reports to Faulk, and no one else works with him, so the records can't separate the two. Kestrel associates log about 2,270 hours a year against 1,940 elsewhere, and they work weekends far more often. Survey comments mention both the weekend workload and humiliating late-night corrections. Some associates also say they under-recorded late-night work, so the hours are probably understated.

My confidence is high on the first point and moderate on the second.

Next steps:
- Don't announce the £12k payment or close the review.
- Commission the confidential outside interviews now. They take about three weeks and cost £9k. Structure them to separate supervision from workload.
- Start tracking matter and supervising partner in attrition reporting.
- Decide on a supervision change or contract reviewers once the interviews are in. Kestrel's review phase ends in December, so the timing is tight.
